tldr: This is a loose topic cluster about running inference on GPUs, not one event. Its main thread is AWS adding managed ways to share one GPU: NVIDIA MIG partitions for SageMaker endpoints on Nov 6, then Lambda GPU functions with up to 48 concurrent invocations per model on Nov 22.
whats_new: An APNIC design guide for self-hosted inference on a few GPU nodes, built on a 4-server, 8-GPU vLLM setup running Llama 3.3 70B, argues that request handling and session count matter more than GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.
why_it_matters: Whether you rent shared GPUs from AWS or run a few nodes yourself, utilization now depends on how requests are batched and routed more than on raw interconnect speed.

beats.headline: SageMaker endpoints can split one GPU with NVIDIA MIG
beats.summary: Hardware-isolated partitions let one GPU host several models or a right-sized slice for one.

beats.headline: Hobby project: a Windows Vulkan GGUF engine written in Delphi
beats.summary: A Hacker News item on local inference, unrelated to the managed-service thread.

beats.headline: Lambda runs GPU inference with 48 concurrent invocations per model
beats.summary: Lambda Managed Instances on G-series GPUs share one loaded model across invocations, with vLLM and SGLang base images.

beats.headline: Self-hosted view: network design for a 4-node, 8-GPU vLLM cluster
beats.summary: For Llama 3.3 70B on a few servers, the guide puts request handling and session count ahead of GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.

open_questions: Which G-series instance types and regions does Lambda GPU support at launch?
How does Lambda GPU pricing compare with a SageMaker endpoint on a MIG partition for the same model?
What cold-start time does a Lambda GPU function show when it loads a model?
Does SageMaker MIG support cover all MIG profiles, or only a fixed set of partition sizes?
At what model size or node count does GPU-to-GPU bandwidth become the bottleneck again for a small vLLM cluster?
take_for_builders: Before buying faster interconnect for a small self-hosted cluster, load-test request concurrency and session counts on vLLM; for bursty small models, benchmark SageMaker MIG and Lambda GPU first.
